prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not give IVIg directly after plasma exchange, and do not give a second IVIg course [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
Do not use succinylcholine for intubation: denervated muscle risks severe hyperkalaemia.
required_recommendations: Intubate and mechanically ventilate in the ICU now: he is in respiratory distress with SpO2 92% on room air and hypercapnia (PaCO2 52 mmHg), MIP -20 cmH2O (weaker than -30), MEP 30 cmH2O (below 40), FVC 41% predicted and a weak cough [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].
Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 28.5 g/day at 71.5 kg) or plasma exchange 200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions: he cannot walk and is 7 days from onset [EAN_PNS_2023].
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring for autonomic instability.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Functional / metabolic brain imaging adds no value in a peripheral demyelinating syndrome.
Cerebrovascular imaging is not indicated in a peripheral neuropathy without focal cerebral signs.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, severe AIDP with secondary axonal injury

differential.key_features: Cannot be excluded at presentation: 7 days of progression fits GBS; reconsider if progression continues beyond 8 weeks or treatment-related fluctuations recur.
CMAP amplitudes are markedly reduced, but distal latencies and conduction velocities are in the demyelinating range, and sensory symptoms with absent sural responses argue against AMAN.
Community onset with no preceding critical illness or ICU stay.
Weakness ascended from the legs after distal paraesthesias, with sensory loss, areflexia and a demyelinating NCS; botulism is descending and purely motor.
No sensory level or sphincter dysfunction; areflexia, facial diplegia and arm weakness place the lesion in the peripheral nerves.

key_clinical_evidence: Rapidly ascending four-limb weakness with global areflexia and facial diplegia 3 weeks after a bloody diarrhoeal illness, with CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 148 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS, meets Brighton level 1 [Brighton_2011].
Respiratory distress with hypoxaemia and hypercapnia means intubation regardless of the spirometry numbers; here MIP -20 and MEP 30 cmH2O are also past the thresholds [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].
Autonomic monitoring is mandatory throughout the acute phase.

The antecedent infection is a history finding; serology is not needed for the diagnosis, and a positive IgM does not prove the trigger. A preceding diarrhoeal illness counts toward a poorer predicted outcome in the modified Erasmus GBS Outcome Score [Walgaard_2011].

general.query: first-line immunotherapy and outcome in severe Guillain-Barre syndrome

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.
The modified Erasmus GBS Outcome Score combines age, preceding diarrhoea and MRC sum score to estimate the chance of walking unaided at 4 weeks and 6 months.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised; outcome can be estimated with the modified EGOS [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021, Walgaard_2011].

specialized_test.impression: Very severe acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with features of secondary axonal injury. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies, severely reduced conduction velocities, markedly reduced CMAP amplitudes, absent sural SNAPs, absent F-waves and H-reflex bilaterally. Findings meet electrodiagnostic criteria for acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy

quantitative_data.pattern: Very severe AIDP with axonal injury

metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions, no red herrings; severe post-diarrhoeal AIDP presenting in respiratory failure that needs immediate intubation.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Seven-day rapidly progressive ascending paralysis and areflexia, preceded by a diarrhoeal illness; SpO2 92% on room air with respiratory distress.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. A. is a 28-year-old restaurant worker presenting with rapidly progressive ascending weakness over 7 days. He had a bloody diarrhoeal illness 3 weeks ago, lasting 5 days (no stool culture obtained). Seven days ago, he noticed tingling in his feet. Weakness ascended rapidly: he could not walk 3 days ago, and now can barely move his legs. Bilateral facial drooping developed 2 days ago. He is now in respiratory distress with SpO2 92% on room air. He is being brought emergently for ICU level care.

neurological_exam.additional: Speaks in short phrases; marked accessory muscle use; weak cough. No paradoxical breathing yet.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral facial diplegia — forehead and lower face both involved. Mild dysarthria. No diplopia.
neurological_exam.motor: Severe bilateral weakness: lower extremity hip flexion 2/5, knee extension 2/5, ankle dorsiflexion 1/5; cannot lift legs off bed. Upper extremity: shoulder abduction 3/5, elbow flexion 3+/5, grip 3+/5 bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral glove-and-stocking paresthesias and numbness to mid-thigh.
